newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Patten hopes Tiananmen crackdown remains on syllabus.
newsitem.headline: Patten hopes Tiananmen crackdown remains on syllabus.

text.p: Governor Chris Patten said on Wednesday he hoped Hong Kong children would continue to be taught about the bloody military crackdown in Beijing in 1989 following the return of the colony to China this year.

"I would hope that today and tomorrow children in Hong Kong, like children in the United Kingdom, would learn about the Opium Wars, would learn about Imperialism in Asia and in China in the 19th century," Patten told a British Broadcasting Corporation (BBC) interview.
"I equally hoped the children would learn about the Great Leap Forward, the Cultural Revolution and what happened in Tiananmen Square in 1989," Patten said.
His comments followed Chinese foreign minister Qian Qichen's recent remarks that Hong Kong textbooks should be revised after the sovereignty change at midnight on June 30.
Britain prised Hong Kong from China a century and a half ago through gunboat diplomacy and the so-called opium wars that were sparked over opium that Western traders were shipping to China.
In June 4, 1989, hundreds, some say thousands, were killed after Chinese military was ordered to end a student-led democracy movement in Beijing's Tiananmen Square.
The Great Leap Forward was a disastrous period of industrialisation in China by the communists in the 1950s while the 1960s Cultural Revolution resulted in great social turmoil.
On Monday, Qian said Hong Kong schoolbooks that do not confirm with China's principles should be revised after the June 30 handover.
Hong Kong's future leader Tung Chee-hwa said on Tuesday he agreed that parts of some school textbooks would need rewriting.
